correctness.rationale: For positive lengths all facet normals are the unit vectors ±e_i and ±(e_i−e_j)/sqrt(2). Coordinate facets have the indicated products of widths; projecting the diagonal into the orthogonal complement of the other d−2 coordinate directions gives the factor sqrt(2)a in the remaining facet areas. The determinant formula gives the volume. With the record's dimensionless variables the quotient reduces to 2^d(d+Bp)^d/[P(1+dp)^(d−1)]. Its logarithmic derivative has the sign of B(1+p)−d(d−1), hence the interior minimum stated in RESULT.md. The normalized Newton inequalities telescope to E_d≤E_2^(d−1), and B≤sqrt(2) binom(d,2), with equality in the latter only for equal normalized lengths. This includes d=2. Substitution yields the stated sharp constant and a/b=sqrt(2)−1. A separate fixed-normal Wulff proof below also recovers the exact constant and equality. evidence: After centering, the zonotope support numbers are (b_i+a)/2 on coordinate normals and (b_i+b_j)/(2 sqrt(2)) on difference normals. Setting all b_i=sqrt(2) and a=2−sqrt(2) makes every support number equal to 1, giving exactly W.

The determinant volume of W is (sqrt(2))^d[1+d(sqrt(2)−1)]. The Wulff bound S≥d V(W)^(1/d) V^(1−1/d) therefore gives the submitted constant. Equality requires homothety to W; the coordinate support numbers force equal b_i and the difference supports then force a=(sqrt(2)−1)b.

evidence: Neumayer defines anisotropic perimeter as the integral of surface tension over exterior unit normals, and gives its sharp Wulff bound and equality up to translation and dilation.
With U={±e_i, ±(e_i−e_j)/sqrt(2)}, take W={x: u·x≤1 for u in U} and tension h_W. Since W contains the unit ball and u itself meets the plane for every u in U, h_W(u)=1 there.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: All tested zonotopes have facet normals in U, so anisotropic perimeter for h_W equals ordinary Euclidean area identically. The associated Wulff body is W; this recasts the claimed optimization as precisely an equality-attaining case of an existing, broader inequality.

value.rationale: The geometric question is natural and the symmetric rigidity is useful to state, but the inequality claimed as the independent finding is mechanically implied once the known tangent configuration is expressed through its fixed facet normals. The facet and determinant formulas are standard evaluations; the alternate Newton proof gives an elementary exposition, not an additional phenomenon or a quantitative stability theorem. No independent valuable remainder requiring a substantive repair was established.
